claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, provided the packet discloses the known mortgage-servicing limitation and accurately describes mitigation as still incomplete.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy.
Current admissible evidence confirms an unresolved named launch use-case limitation.
Policy requires disclosure of that limitation unless it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Draft monitoring intent is not equivalent to an approved mitigation under the stated policy text.
A compliant certification record would need either evidence that the weakness is no longer material/current or approved mitigation/risk acceptance satisfying the policy elements.
evidence_requests: Approved risk-acceptance record covering the mortgage servicing hardship-forbearance limitation, if one exists.
Final model-card language disclosing the limitation and its scope.
Approved mitigation/runbook showing accountable owner, alert threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Materiality determination for the unresolved slice issue and who approved it.
specific_concerns: A named launch use-case slice remains below target in hardship forbearance explanation.
The current model-card draft says there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the unresolved slice issue.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because the alert threshold and accountable owner are still TBD.
The policy text requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for certification without material caveats.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or a fully approved mitigation package that satisfies the policy predicates.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action `certify_model` is not fully supported as an unqualified certification on the current record.
Any implication that the mitigation is already sufficient to remove the current disclosure requirement is unsupported.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and no severity-one incidents alone satisfy the certification threshold is unsupported given the unresolved named use-case limitation.
